notes: F3 IN ISOLATION, baseline scanner-2026-07-28-luna-c (run 3). FAILED — F3 is to be reverted. Change: a class_sweep array declared BEFORE findings in the strict schema, a prompt procedure requiring one verdict per assigned class before any finding, and five mechanical invariants per lane in a new class-sweep.json. THE MECHANISM WORKED AND CHANGED NOTHING: 541/541 lanes swept, 3005/3005 lane-class pairs (100%), zero missing/offlist/duplicate/inconsistent/found_without_finding. FILE_ONLY did not move at all, 13 -> 13. Per-class coverage went from an implicit ~17% to an explicit 100% and converted no entry. The hypothesis that FILE_ONLY is a sweep-coverage failure is FALSIFIED, which retires the whole prompt-sequencing family of interventions for it. Regression: HIT 49 -> 29, CATEGORY_MISS 3 -> 21, findings 407 -> 311, producing lanes 250 -> 202, utilisation 0.310 -> 0.267. The stated revert criterion was 'utilisation rises but FILE_ONLY does not'; utilisation FELL, so revert is unambiguous. TWO MECHANISMS. (1) The sweep gated rather than checked: inconsistent_classes and found_without_finding are both 0 everywhere, so verdicts and labels moved in lockstep; requiring that any class in a finding be swept 'found' turned a cheap early 'absent' into a hard block on labelling it later. Only 372/3005 pairs (12.4%) came back 'found' against run 3's 503 (16.7%) actually emitted -- the explicit pass is MORE conservative than the implicit one it replaced. crypto-auth 19/25 -> 1/25. (2) F3 also deleted the anti-suppression nudge and replaced it with text legitimising empty output -- a SECOND VARIABLE inside a change billed as single-variable, so part of the regression is not attributable to the sweep. Keep the instrumentation but make it non-binding. Stages 0 and 0.5 were reused from run 3 unchanged and md5-verified before launch, so the lane manifest is identical across runs 2, 3 and 4. Metrics on the 97-reachable basis.

notes: Run 5. Three playbook edits, all acting on class attribution: injection gains cross-site scripting (reflected/stored/DOM, stored reported at the persistence point); ssrf gains open redirect and weak destination allow-listing; crypto-auth gains an authentication-outcome anchor. Merged as PR #22. Stage 0/0.5 carried over from run 3 unchanged so the comparison is single-variable. RESULT: localization 75.3% -> 80.4% (best recorded); FILE_ONLY bucket 13 -> 2; injection-class localization 18/18 and ssrf-class 3/3, both as predicted by the pre-run arm. Hedging FELL 1.538 -> 1.518, so the localization gain is not a wider net. CAVEAT ON THE RECALL NUMBER: recall fell 50.5% -> 43.3%, and that drop is NOT a detection regression. Three ground-truth lines carry 24 of the 97 reachable entries; run 3 won 24/24 of them and run 5 won 16/24, which is -8 entries and accounts for the whole delta. Excluding those three lines, recall is 34.2% -> 35.6% (flat) and localization is 67.1% -> 74.0% (+6.9pp, best of any run). See the run archive MANIFEST and docs/analysis/2026-07-29-localization-investigation.md. The pre-run projection (localization ~86.6%, recall ~56.7%) was too optimistic on both: it assumed +11 net localization where the run delivered +11 gained and 6 lost, and assumed the anchor would hold ~22/24 hot-line entries where it held 16/24.
